chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of women who rode the mounts are the women of Quraysh — most compassionate toward children and the best to a husband.'

key_terms.أَحْنَاهُ: ahna — superlative of hanan (compassion/tenderness), the most compassionate
key_terms.الرِّحَالَ: al-rihal — saddles/mounts, idiomatically referring to women who travel to marry
key_terms.قُرَيْشٍ: Quraysh — the noble Arab tribe of the Prophet; also the name of Surah 106 of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the women of Quraysh in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a statement from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) praising the women of the tribe of Quraysh — the Prophet's own tribe — for two virtues: their compassion and tenderness toward their children, and their excellence as wives. The expression 'rode the mounts' (rakibna al-rihal) is an idiomatic reference to women who traveled to their husbands' homes upon marriage. This narration reflects the pre-Islamic Arabian cultural context where riding to a new household upon marriage was a common practice, and Quraysh women were held in high regard both for their noble lineage and their domestic virtues.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The best of the women who rode the rides (to the houses of their husbands) are the women of Qureysh, being compassionate upon children and the best for a husband’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘The best of women who ever rode a camel on their wedding to the house of their husband are the women of Quraysh who are most compassionate to their children and are the best of them for their husband. 5 ”
